findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: The handler was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` with a stub `evaluate` to `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` is an `abc.ABC` with abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and none are implemented here. `Detector.detector_handler` does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` instead of returning an empty result. Because `process_detectors` iterates detectors without a try/except, one such detector would abort processing for the whole list. Either keep the previous concrete stub, or implement the abstract methods. The TODO comment above the class is also stale, since it says this will become stateful later.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The PR changes the return type of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This is misleading, since the dict keying is the point of the change (to prevent duplicate results per group key).

findings.title: New abstract hook has no docstring or contract
findings.body: `build_occurrence_and_event_data` is a new public extension point for subclasses, but it has no docstring. Implementers get no guidance on what `value` is, that `new_status` is never OK (OK produces a StatusChangeMessage instead), or what `event_data` must contain. The `event_data` requirements for `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` are non-obvious, such as `project_id`, `event_id`, `timestamp` and `platform`.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests cannot detect a wrongly passed value
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it. The tests then build expectations with a hardcoded `6` even when the evaluated value is 100, 8 or 10 (for example `test_results_on_change`, `test_dedupe` and `test_state_results_multi_group` for group_2). If `evaluate_group_key_value` passed the wrong value to the hook, these tests would still pass. The tests only verify `group_key` (via the fingerprint) and `new_status`. Encoding `value` into the mock occurrence, for example in `evidence_data`, and using the real value in expectations would give the hook argument real coverage.
